rows.answer: Nike had approximately **77,800 employees worldwide** as of **May 31, 2025**, the end of fiscal 2025, including retail and part-time employees. [1]

Nike’s effective tax rate rose to **17.1% in fiscal 2025 from 14.9% in fiscal 2024**, a **220-basis-point increase**. The main reasons were:

- A less favorable **earnings mix**;
- **Lower benefits from stock-based compensation**; and
- The absence of certain **one-time tax benefits recognized in fiscal 2024**, including relief related to U.S. foreign tax-credit regulations.

These increases were partially offset by a **$133 million one-time, non-cash deferred tax benefit** in fiscal 2025 related to U.S. tax rules for foreign-currency gains and losses. [1][2]

Converse revenues declined to **$1.692 billion in fiscal 2025 from $2.082 billion in fiscal 2024**, a **19% reported decrease** and **18% currency-neutral decrease**. The decline was driven by lower revenues across all territories: **unit sales fell 12%**, while lower average selling prices reduced revenue by approximately **6 percentage points**, primarily because of higher discounts in direct-to-consumer sales. [1][2]

By channel, **wholesale revenue decreased 20% currency-neutral**, particularly in Western Europe and Asia, while **direct-to-consumer revenue decreased 17%** because of reduced traffic across all territories and lower average selling prices from higher discounts. [1]

Nike had used approximately **66.7%** of its **$18 billion** share repurchase program by **May 31, 2025**, based on approximately **$12.0 billion** repurchased under the program: $12.0 billion ÷ $18.0 billion × 100 = 66.7%. [1][2]
Lululemon employed **approximately 39,000 people worldwide** at the end of fiscal 2024, which ended **February 2, 2025**. [1]
Lululemon’s company-operated stores grew by **7.9%** in fiscal 2024, increasing from **711 stores as of January 28, 2024, to 767 as of February 2, 2025**. [1][2]

Lululemon’s Americas business accounted for **74.9% of 2024 net revenue**—approximately **$7.93 billion of $10.59 billion**. [1] The annual report also states this represented **75%** of total net revenue. [2]

Lululemon’s MIRROR acquisition was effectively wound down. Acquired in July 2020 and rebranded as lululemon Studio, MIRROR’s hardware sales and digital app-only subscriptions were discontinued in 2023; Lululemon stopped selling the Studio Mirror and new digital-content subscriptions in December 2023. It instead partnered with Peloton as the exclusive digital-fitness content provider for existing subscribers. [1][2]

The business generated substantial write-downs: Lululemon recorded a **$362.5 million goodwill impairment** and **$40.6 million impairment of MIRROR-related intangible assets** in fiscal 2022, followed by **$44.2 million of asset impairments** and **$30.3 million of restructuring costs** in fiscal 2023. [3] In fiscal 2024, it disposed of the remaining Studio Mirror inventory. [4]
Under Armour held **$501.361 million in cash and cash equivalents** at the end of fiscal 2025 (**March 31, 2025**). [1]

Under Armour’s selling, general and administrative expenses **increased by 8.4%** in fiscal 2025, from **$2,400,502 thousand in fiscal 2024 to $2,601,991 thousand in fiscal 2025** (year ended March 31, 2025). [1]

Under Armour’s operating cash flow fell by **$413.3 million**, from **$354.0 million in fiscal 2024 to $(59.3) million in fiscal 2025** (years ended March 31) [1][2]. The primary reason was a **$455.5 million decline in net income before non-cash items**, as the company moved from **$232.0 million of net income to a $201.3 million net loss** [1][2].

Working-capital changes partially offset the decline by **$42.2 million**, but still included cash outflows from **inventories ($205.5 million), other non-current assets ($76.7 million), and accrued expenses and other liabilities ($44.4 million)**; these were partly offset by inflows from accounts payable and accounts receivable [1].

Under Armour sold its MapMyFitness digital platform during the second quarter of Fiscal 2025, so it was no longer part of Under Armour’s digital-platform operations afterward. [1][2] The sale generated proceeds and a **$5.3 million gain** for Under Armour. [3][4]
Columbia Sportswear had approximately **9,780 employees** as of **December 31, 2024**. [1]
Columbia Sportswear’s share repurchases increased by **72.7%**, from **$184.0 million in 2023** to **$317.8 million in 2024** (fiscal years ended December 31) [1].

Columbia Sportswear’s effective income tax rate was **25.1% in 2024**, compared with **22.9% in 2023**—an increase of **2.2 percentage points**. [1][2] The 2024 rate included a non-recurring valuation allowance expense, while 2023 included non-recurring tax benefits. [1][2]

Columbia Sportswear’s U.S. wholesale customer base is relatively diversified: it has **over 1,850 U.S. wholesale customers**. In fiscal 2024, its **five largest U.S. wholesale customers accounted for approximately 20% of U.S. net sales**, with **no individual customer accounting for 10% or more** [1].

Thus, the company has **moderate concentration among its largest customers, but no individually dominant U.S. wholesale customer**.

Deckers’ ten largest customers accounted for **23.7% of fiscal 2025 net sales** [1][2]. Based on total net sales of **$4,985.612 million** for the year ended March 31, 2025, this equals approximately **$1,181.6 million**.
Deckers’ international net sales grew **26.3% in fiscal 2025** (fiscal year ended March 31, 2025), reaching **$1,798,903 thousand**, compared with **$1,424,089 thousand** in fiscal 2024. [1][2]

Deckers **sold the Sanuk brand and certain related assets** to a buyer; the transaction was completed on **August 15, 2024**, during fiscal 2025 (year ended March 31, 2025). [1] Deckers did not classify Sanuk as discontinued operations because it determined the divestiture was not a strategic shift with a major effect on consolidated results. [1]

Deckers carried out a **six-for-one forward stock split** on **September 13, 2024**, during fiscal 2025. Each outstanding share was automatically split into six shares; trading on a split-adjusted basis began September 17, 2024. [1][2]
